result.summary: This PR adds an optional `precious` flag to the IPC Mining interface's `submitBlock` and `submitSolution` methods, so a caller can atomically submit a block and prefer it over a same-work competing tip in one IPC call, instead of calling `submitblock` followed by a separate `preciousblock` RPC. It refactors `ActivateBestChain` to expose an internal `ActivateBestChain_` helper so `PreciousBlock` can call it while already holding `m_chainstate_mutex`, and changes `PreciousBlock`'s signature to report whether the block ended up connected. It also extracts a shared `GrindBlock` test helper to deduplicate proof-of-work grinding loops across many unit tests, and adds unit and functional coverage for the new precious behavior.
result.problem: IPC mining clients currently need two round trips (submitBlock then preciousblock RPC) to submit and prefer a same-work side block, and the existing PreciousBlock/ActivateBestChain interaction has a potential race between PreciousBlock's read of chain state and a concurrent chain activation. This affects developers building mining software on the IPC interface and anyone reasoning about PreciousBlock's correctness.

Sjors: raises a game-theory caveat that preferring your own block may not always be rational for miners to build on, relevant to how the feature should be exposed; no resolution reached.
Sjors: miner_tests.cpp additions are large and should be split or interleaved differently; unaddressed.

result.card: This draft PR adds an optional `precious` flag to the IPC Mining interface's submitBlock and submitSolution methods, letting external miners atomically submit and prefer a same-work side block instead of making a separate preciousblock RPC call, and refactors ActivateBestChain/PreciousBlock chainstate locking to make the result race-free. It solves a real but narrow convenience gap for IPC mining clients (no named external consumer yet), while its ActivateBestChain_ extraction and PreciousBlock locking change touch validation's chainstate-activation path in a way that deserves independent scrutiny. Sjors gave Concept ACK but flagged that `precious` probably should not change duplicate-block reporting, and raised a game-theory concern about whether miners should prefer their own block at all; the author has not responded in 55 days. The PR needs a rebase, is still marked draft, and depends on the earlier PR #34644 it says it is built on top of.
